scope: Independent review of A148 original-byte predicate/write behavior under synthetic MMIO. The observed register store does not establish physical command meaning.
checks: Independently decoded the exact 56-byte body A148..A180 from the pinned firmware with Thumb-MCLASS Capstone. The code confirms R0==1 with unsigned R1<=1, else UXTB(R0-2)<=1 and R1==0; the UXTB makes the second acceptance depend on the low byte of the subtraction.

The write expression follows LSL R0,6 then AND 0xFF, OR R1&0x3F, OR 0x40000000, and a single STR to literal 0x40010000. Rejections load 0x004A0001 or 0x004A0002 and return through BX LR; accepted calls return zero. No helper or stack frame appears in the body.

Reran all 54 original-byte inputs from an isolated output directory; regenerated rows match the candidate exactly. This includes 258/259 aliases with R1=0 and rejection boundaries including 257, 0xFFFFFFFF, R1=64, and invalid mode/selector pairs.
Accepted cases produce one 32-bit write; rejected cases produce none and preserve the synthetic MMIO word. SP remains unchanged.
limitations: The test maps a synthetic register region and observes instruction-level writes only; it cannot establish hardware command semantics, timing, or peripheral response.
Only fixture-selected inputs were replayed. This is private P2 evidence, not canonical admission or proof that callers reach the routine.
